substance.name: Indoxacarb (enantiomeric reaction mass S:R 75:25)
substance.notes: Signals are the analyst layer; summary and sources are the evidence layer. Plant-protection events under Reg. (EC) 1107/2009 are tagged 'ppp' and are a separate regime. Records merged by topic, so a single record may span several acts. Data pulls: active substances 2026-09-01 (db updated 2026-08-31), products 2026-09-03.

records.title: Renewal filed — but France routed it to full evaluation
records.summary: Application under Article 13(1). On 12 November 2018 France decided a full Article 14(1) evaluation was necessary, triggering the 365-day Article 8(1) clock.

signal.label: Moderate
signal.rationale: Rules out lapse by non-application. Offset by the full-evaluation route.

sources.citation: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/731, recitals 2–3; Decision (EU) 2019/1030, recitals 2–3; Decision (EU) 2021/1287, recitals 2–3
sources.pinpoint: Recitals on submission and on the Article 14(1) decision
sources.note: CONFLICT between the Commission's own acts: 2019/1030 and 2024/731 both state 28 June 2018; 2021/1287 states 26 June 2018. Two primary acts to one, so 28 June adopted here. A secondary source (useforesight.io) also gives 28 June. The 26 June date used in earlier versions of this log was wrong.

records.title: PPP approval not renewed on mammal risk; reference values cut
records.summary: Reg. (EU) 2021/2081, ground: high long-term risk to small herbivorous mammals. Withdrawal by 19/03/2022, grace to 19/09/2022. ADI cut from 0.006 to 0.005 mg/kg bw/day, ARfD from 0.125 to 0.005 mg/kg bw.

signal.label: Strong
signal.rationale: Mammal risk is spray-specific and does not transfer to indoor baits. The lowered reference values are substance-level and do. No source shows the biocidal file citing either.

sources.note: Preceded by Directive 2006/10/EC inclusion and EFSA conclusions of 2018 (J. 5140) and 2019 (J. 5866).

records.title: France names the blockers: substance identity and endocrine disruption testing needed
records.summary: The eCA reported the evaluation delayed by the need to assess reference specifications and endocrine-disrupting properties, and expected to submit the renewal assessment report in Q2 2024.

signal.label: Strong
signal.rationale: Reference specifications go to the 75:25 identity; ED is both an exclusion ground and a substitution criterion. France did not treat EFSA's 2018 'ED unlikely' finding as settling it.

sources.pinpoint: Recital recording the eCA notification of 19 September 2023

sources.note: CONFLICT: PPP peer review concluded ED unlikely; the biocidal eCA is assessing it independently.

records.title: GB retains PT18 approval to 31/01/2027 — no biocidal divergence
records.summary: GB expiry postponed to 30/06/2025, then covered by HSE's blanket extension of actives expiring 01/01/2024–31/12/2026 to 31 January 2027. GB separately moved to withdraw the PPP approval.

signal.label: Moderate
signal.rationale: Both regimes keep biocidal and ended PPP. GB has a general instrument covering the gap; the EU has none.

sources.citation: HSE, ministerial decisions under the GB Biocidal Products Regulation
HSE draft decision to withdraw GB plant protection approval (Article 21(1))
sources.note: PPP file; relies on Reg. 2021/2081 and the revised reference values.

records.title: Field resistance is eroding every bait active, indoxacarb included
records.summary: 102 German cockroach resistance studies across 23 countries and 60 actives. A California field study found increased survivorship toward fipronil, clothianidin, indoxacarb, emamectin benzoate and hydramethylnon alike. A VGSC V1848I strain showed 146-fold indoxacarb and 431-fold metaflumizone resistance.

signal.label: Neutral or mixed
signal.rationale: Efficacy is eroding, but indoxacarb's value as an IRAC 22A rotation partner is the standard retention argument. Neither is a renewal criterion.

sources.citation: Rahayu et al., Trop. Life Sci. Res. 2025;36(3):15
Lee, Choe, Rust & Lee, J. Econ. Entomol. 2022;115(1):259
